threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can always spot a newbie by their bewildered face at the bus stop, staring at the route map like it's a cryptic puzzle.
Last night on the 118, a guy serenaded the entire bus with Adele. Surprisingly, everyone joined in for the chorus; felt like a weird, joyful karaoke night.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a stray cat lounging on my balcony, perfectly content, while I was struggling with IKEA furniture. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever seen a U-Bahn train graffiti'd with a full-on vintage movie poster? Only in Friedrichshain, where art isn't just in galleries, it's on the tracks.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You spot a true local if they know which taco truck at 24th always runs out of al pastor by 7 PM. The newcomers just stand there confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a guy serenading the bus stop with a ukulele while a pigeon tried to join in. Only in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most think Gràcia is just about the bohemian vibe, but they miss the silent, sun-drenched corners where the locals sip coffee, not cocktails.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll see them struggling with the 'universal' metro card, fumbling at the machines while locals glide through like pros.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Tube is a quick way to get around? Wait 'til you try catching a bus at peak hour—that's the real Hackney experience.
Caught the N37 last night, and a guy started arguing with a pigeon in the middle of the road. Not sure who was winning.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting at the park, I saw a grandma teaching her grandson to skateboard while a group was setting up their open-air cinema. Pure Neukölln vibes.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you'll find spontaneous parties in abandoned buildings, complete with local DJs spinning vinyl. It's not just a party; it's a whole experience of Berlin's DIY culture.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their patience at BART delays. A tourist's just confused; a local rolls their eyes and checks their phone.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today, driver turned up the music—everyone started singing along. For a moment, chaos felt like a community jam session.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love the vermut bars, but many of us prefer a quiet pastís at home instead of the crowded terraces.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can usually tell by the way they still attempt to pronounce 'Glòries' as 'glories' instead of just a quick 'glo-ree-es' like the locals.
